Last month, after the shutdown of the TV tracking app TV Time, one of the app's co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and television tracking app called Bingers, emphasizing its social features. Here are the relevant details.

Bingers is now available for download

The film and TV tracking app TV Time was previously announced by Whip Media to be shutting down. One of its co-founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioned as a "fast, beautiful, and fun community-driven watchlist."

Now, according to TechCrunch, Bingers is available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering a kind of "spiritual successor" for users still searching for a TV Time alternative — TV Time was once one of the most widely used TV tracking apps in the world.

Users who were formerly TV Time users and have saved their data through the export tools provided by the platform before the app was shut down can import their archives into Bingers, allowing for a seamless transition to continue using the service; as for users who never exported their data, or new users who have never used a TV tracking app, they can start building their records from scratch.

Bingers strongly emphasizes its community-driven features, such as user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity elections. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features were precisely what allowed TV Time to remain popular over time:

For users who simply want to track the shows and movies they have watched, Bingers provides dedicated watchlists and viewing history. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays a schedule of upcoming shows and premiere dates, with a countdown of how many days remain until release.

Bingers is available for free on the App Store, and currently does not offer in-app purchases.
